drivingQuestion: What novel case does 'if due to the robber he is liable' teach?
outcomeNote: The question is answered in the next unit (לא צריכא, דאחוי אחווי)

segments.he: אִם מֵחֲמַת הַגַּזְלָן – חַיָּיב. הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּאַנְסוּהָ לְאַרְעָא דִידֵיהּ וְלָא אֲנַסוּה כּוּלֵּי אַרְעָתָא, הָא מֵרֵישָׁא שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ: אִם מַכַּת מְדִינָה הִיא כּוּ׳, אִי לָא – לָא!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «If» the thugs took the field «due to the robber,» the robber is «obligated» to provide the owner with a different field. The Gemara asks: «What are the circumstances» of the case in the latter clause of the mishna? «If we say» that «they seized» only «his land,» i.e., the robber’s land, «and did not seize all» the other «lands» in the region, «you already learned this from the first clause» of the mishna: «If it is a regional disaster» in which the thugs seize all the property in the region, the robber is not obligated to compensate the owner of the field, which indicates that «if it is not» a regional disaster, the robber is «not» exempt from payment. What novelty does the latter clause teach?
